reason: Verified in the live accessibility tree, not just the source. render-b.js:1673 sets role="status" on the <section class="b-field" aria-label="The plan for Mara & Finn">. Chromium's full AX tree confirms both consequences. (1) The landmark is destroyed on exactly one screen: loading-slow exposes 'status :: The plan for Mara & Finn'; loading, ended, phone, day, desk, print, publish, owner-empty, owner-editing, owner-undone and owner-flight all expose 'region :: The plan for ...'. The only screen where the audience meets failure is the only one that loses the landmark. (2) The status node computes live="polite", atomic=true, relevant="additions text". Every write inside it therefore re-reads the entire field, whose innerText is 'MARA & FINN TODAY IS 16 JULY This is taking longer than it should. The plan has not been deleted, and the link still works. Try again' (132 chars, not the finding's 137 - the only inaccuracy, and immaterial). The retry handler writes says.textContent twice, toggles note.style.display twice and flips aria-busy, so the whole screen is re-read at the person who just pressed the button inside it. The code does contradict its own comment nine lines below, verbatim: 'A live region of its own. The .b-field cannot serve as one: it contains the button being pressed, so announcing through it re-reads the whole screen back at the person who pressed it.' The .b-field does contain the Try again button. There is a second harm the finding does not name: the handler sets aria-busy="true" on the field, which is now a live-region root containing .b-live, so the round-7 announcement is at risk of being held by its own ancestor's busy flag - removing the role removes that ambiguity too. Not already handled: role="status" is present in the generated master. Not load-bearing: nothing in interaction-check.mjs reads the field's role - line 440 checks .b-undo, line 1100 checks .b-live, and lines 2210/2512 read aria-busy only. Not a gate restatement: the accessibility-spine loop at interaction-check.mjs:258 iterates only ["phone","desk","print","owner-flight","day"], so 'the plan is a region' and 'exactly one h1' have never been run against loading-slow. The publish rider is also true: publish carries zero h1 in .tl-stage, its .b-pressTitle standing as an H2 at 38px/390 and 48px/1440 with no heading above it. Fix verified by simulation: removing the role attribute in-page restored 'region :: The plan for Mara & Finn' while retry still marked busy true, wrote 'Trying again.' then 'Still not arriving. The plan has not been deleted, and the link still works.' to .b-live, swapped .b-sub both ways, and kept focus on [data-act=retry] - every existing loading-slow assertion still passes. Real, specific, nothing lost, and it is a defect on the screen that matters most.
sharpenedFix: Delete `field.setAttribute("role", "status");` from states["loading-slow"] in render-b.js; aria-busy already marks the wait and .b-live is the announcer, and the region landmark returns. Then close the coverage hole that let it live: extend the state list at interaction-check.mjs:258 to ["phone","desk","print","owner-flight","day","publish","owner-empty","loading","loading-slow","owner-editing","owner-undone","ended"] (leave unfurl out - it is a link-preview card with no .b-field and no heading, and would fail both assertions for the right reason), and add `ok('the field is not itself a live region - ' + state, !document.querySelector('.b-field[role="status"]'))`. Publish will then fail 'exactly one h1'; promote `h("h2.b-pressTitle", ...)` to `h("h1.b-pressTitle", ...)` in states.publish, which matches what the screen already looks like at 38/48px. Note the h1-names-the-project assertion already passes for publish ('Mara & Finn have had this since ...') and for ended ('This link has ended.') it does not - either widen that regex or drop ended from the added list.
